To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the visual and textual analysis of the rendered page can provide a sufficient amount of information for the extraction of a particular information from the web page, and that this approach is robust enough to handle the variety of HTML code used in the Semantic Publishing Challenge.

the information extraction task can be solved in a generic way by analyzing the rendered page content rather than its HTML code, and that the RDF-based model is a suitable way to represent the page contents and to combine the results from different analysis methods.
the visual and textual features are useful for the information extraction from web pages and that the layout of the pages can help to improve the extraction results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How to represent web pages for information extraction?
the following questions: (i) how can we represent the page content for further processing, and (ii) how can we extract the information of interest from it using a set of rules.
the following questions: (i) what kind of information can we extract from the rendered web pages?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is able to extract a large amount of information from the web pages, but it is not always able to extract the information with high precision.
the approach proposed in the present paper is a good example of how to extract information from the web pages with an invalid or semantically incomplete HTML code.
the proposed approach has shown to be effective and efficient for the given task, however, the further research should be conducted to improve it in terms of accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a method for extracting the information from a web page based on the analysis of its rendered content.
we have proposed a method for extracting information from the web pages that does not require any semantic annotation of their code.
we propose a method that allows to extract information from web pages without any knowledge of their HTML code and without the need of the page authors to use specific HTML tags for this purpose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information extraction from web pages can be done without the need for a full page structure analysis.
the information extraction can be performed in a more robust and efficient manner by using the rendered pages instead of the HTML code.
the information extraction task can be solved in an efficient way by combining different analysis techniques and using a generic rule-based approach to the extraction.
